title: Measures to Address Recent Spate of Lift Breakdowns at HDB Blocks
what_it_is: Measures to Address Recent Spate of Lift Breakdowns at HDB Blocks

sections.label: Questions on lift maintenance rules
sections.summary: MPs asked the Minister for National Development about lift breakdown ceilings, BCA audits, procurement criteria, training, and Town Council costs and grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry will consider specifying a ceiling rate for lift breakdowns or a maximum period in which the breakdown rate consistently exceeds 0.1 such that the lift company that fails to meet the standard will be barred from operations; and (b) whether the Ministry will statutorily require lift companies to professionally train and certify their lift installation and maintenance workers before deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) what is the progress on the independent audit checks of passenger lifts by BCA; (b) what are some of the key findings so far; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider a new lift upgrading programme to help Town Councils replace older lifts that experience frequent breakdowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked	 the Minister for National Development whether the Ministry will consider (i) tightening the criteria of lift procurements; (ii) embarking on an open system specification, requiring potential lift suppliers bidding for HDB projects to facilitate use of common parts for their lifts; and (iii) setting up a lift expert team in BCA or to better regulate lift maintenance companies and working with the industry to build up sufficient lift maintenance staff to service the lifts in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) what is the expected additional cost to Town Councils as a result of BCA's new standards on lift maintenance; (b) whether HDB will provide specific lift-maintenance grants to Town Councils as a result of BCA's modified regime; and (c) whether HDB will consider a subsidy or co-payment scheme for HDB lift parts that turn obsolete prematurely.

sections.label: HDB lift breakdown rates
sections.summary: Tele-Monitoring System data show about 20 breakdowns per 1,000 HDB lifts monthly in 2015 and the first half of this year, lower than 30 in 2013 and 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Data from the Tele-Monitoring System (TMS), which provides real-time monitoring of HDB lifts, indicate 	Page: 15 that there were around 20 breakdowns per 1,000 lifts every month in 2015, and the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This is lower than the average breakdown rate of 30 per 1,000 lifts each month registered in the previous two years, in 2013 and 2014.

sections.label: New lift breakdown requirement
sections.summary: HDB requires new lifts in BTO projects and the Lift Upgrading Programme to have not more than one breakdown per month per 10 lifts during the one-year Defects Liability Period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For new lifts installed in BTO projects and under the Lift Upgrading Programme, HDB imposes the requirement of not more than one lift breakdown per month per 10 lifts installed during the one-year Defects Liability Period (DLP).

sections.label: Common lift parts access
sections.summary: The Competition Commission is looking into ensuring third-party lift maintenance contractors have access to essential lift spare parts, which the Minister agreed with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In this regard, Mr Ang Wei Neng suggested that we facilitate the use of common parts for lifts so that Town Councils will have more contractor options to choose from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I agree with him and I would like to share that the Competition Commission is looking into this very matter, to ensure that third-party lift maintenance contractors have access to essential lift spare parts.

sections.label: Town Council lift funding plans
sections.summary: MND intends to require Town Councils to set aside more S&CC collections into Sinking Funds and ring-fence part for lift replacement, with no plans to extend the SLRP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Town Councils must project and plan ahead and ensure sufficient savings for long-term financial sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why MND intends to require all Town Councils to set aside a higher proportion of their S&CC collections into their Sinking Funds and to ring-fence a part of the Sinking Fund specifically for lift replacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The SLRP is a one-off programme and we do not have plans to extend it further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The replacement of old lifts is the responsibility of the Town Councils and ought to be undertaken by them as part of their cyclical maintenance programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: However, for the existing lifts that are not due for replacement soon, we will look at the possibility of helping the Town Councils retrofit them with key safety enhancements and features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, I am not talking about lifts that are due for replacement because these are old lifts that should be replaced by the Town Councils; but about the ones that are not due for replacement soon, MND will look at the possibility of helping Town Councils retrofit them with key safety enhancements and features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This support for safety enhancements for existing lifts will require significant Government expenditure, so we are studying the matter carefully and will announce the details when ready.

sections.label: Liquidated damages for lift contractors
sections.summary: Current liquidated damages imposed on lift contractors for service recovery delays and maintenance non-compliance amount to only $50 per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Let us work together to make it even better and safer for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I understand that current liquidated damages imposed on lift contractors for delays in service recovery and non-compliance with maintenance standards only amount to $50 per day.

sections.label: Lift breakdown rates fall
sections.summary: Lift breakdown rates fell from 30 to 20 per 1,000 lifts between 2013 and today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: My purpose of mentioning it was to show that over the period of time from 2013 till today, the breakdown rates have fallen from 30 to 20 per 1,000 lifts.

sections.label: Longer Defects Liability Period considered
sections.summary: A longer Defects Liability Period beyond the current one-year DLP may potentially be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On his suggestion about making sure there is a longer Defects Liability Period (DLP), meaning to say, after procuring and installing the lifts, would we want the contractor to have a requirement to maintain the lift for a longer period beyond the one-year DLP which is in place today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will look at it and we potentially can consider a longer DLP.

sections.label: BCA audit and permit certification
sections.summary: BCA will undertake a new permit to operate the system, displayed and renewed annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But beyond that, were there any other findings from BCA's 	Page: 18 independent audit since March?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But last Friday, the Commissioner issued new instructions to say that a new permit to operate the system will be undertaken by BCA and this certification will be required to be displayed and renewed annually.

sections.label: Older lifts higher breakdown rate
sections.summary: Older lifts, particularly those beyond 20 years, tend to have a higher breakdown rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Generally, if you look at data, like from the TMS and if you look at the overall state of lifts today, we can say that older lifts tend to have a higher breakdown rate, in particular, older lifts beyond 20 years.

sections.label: Display requirement in broader review
sections.summary: Requiring display is part of a broader review to tighten standards and ensure accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The decision now to require it to be displayed is really part of the broader review to see how we can tighten standards and ensure accountability.

sections.label: Study on Town Council finances
sections.summary: A study is ongoing and Town Councils will be informed about safety enhancements and lift vintage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Town Councils will have to start determining how to project their finances going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we are doing a study right now and we will be informing Town Councils in due course what we intend to do for the safety enhancements and what vintage of lifts.

sections.label: Lift replacement period guideline
sections.summary: Lifts in other countries have operated for more than 30, 40, 50 years, so the replacement period is simply a guideline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are lifts in other countries that have been operating for more than 30, 40, 50 years and still continuing to operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the point about the replacement period, it is simply a guideline.

sections.label: Tightening lift certification
sections.summary: The Member suggested certification, and the speaker says they are going to tighten it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the earlier point that the Member has suggested on certification, we are going to tighten.

sections.label: Contractor responsibility and future tenders
sections.summary: If the contractor is responsible, HDB will consider this and its past records before awarding future lift tenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If, indeed, the contractor is the one who is responsible, then this will be taken 	Page: 21 into account the next time the contractor submits a bid for a future HDB lift contract and HDB will look at its past records and consider it very carefully before awarding it any future tenders.

sections.label: Town Councils real-time fault data
sections.summary: All Town Councils today have access to real-time fault data of every lift in their housing estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: All Town Councils today – if Members do not already realise this – have access to real-time fault data of every lift in your housing estate.

sections.label: Tightening procurement, testing, commissioning
sections.summary: They will tighten processes of procurement, testing and commissioning of lifts before taking over lifts from the contractor.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Otherwise, later on, whatever maintenance we do, the fault will be very difficult to rectify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They will be tightening on their processes of not just procurement but testing and commissioning of lifts, before taking over the lifts from the contractor.

sections.label: BCA technical team and expert panel
sections.summary: BCA has been building a strong technical team and will continue, and has been asked to get advice from an independent panel of local and foreign experts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: BCA, as the lift authority in Singapore, has already, over the years, been building up a strong technical team and will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I have also asked BCA to get advice from an independent panel of experts, who could be local and foreign.
